clue.text: Is he going in to discover it's all done?

indicators.note: the words 'Is he' are going in, entering the word for discover

parts.note: to discover is to find
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a man's entrance reveals that the job is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completed with nothing left to do is finished, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Commercial set in new cafe may give a false impression

indicators.note: the commercial is set inside the rearranged letters of cafe
making the word cafe new means rearranging its letters

parts.note: a commercial on television is an ad

explanation.surface: An advert placed in a newly opened cafe might mislead customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun for an advert; 'new' rearranges the four letters to FACE before 'set in' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: A front put on to hide the truth gives a deceptive outward appearance, the figurative sense of a building's front.

clue.text: Papal ambassador about to be accepted by new union

indicators.note: the short word for about is taken in, accepted, by the reworked letters of union
a new form of the word union is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: C, for circa, is the Latin abbreviation meaning about

explanation.surface: A Vatican diplomat is about to be welcomed into a newly formed union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns UNION into NUNIO, and 'accepted by' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's diplomatic representative to a foreign government is called a nuncio.

clue.text: It smells awful when it goes off

definitions.text: It smells awful when it goes off

parts.words: It smells awful when it goes off
parts.note: goes off suggests food turning bad, but here it means a prank device being set off and releasing a stench

explanation.surface: Something that stinks once it spoils, like old milk or meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' reads as spoiling food; it is a joke-shop device exploding into a foul smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank capsule that releases a foul odour when broken is described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Bold break-in using a jemmy?

definitions.meaning: bold means daring and full of initiative
read as two words, getting in while levering with a crowbar: entering by prising

explanation.surface: A daring burglary carried out with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is a burglar's short crowbar; split the answer into ENTER and PRISING for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bold and resourceful in starting ventures is described with this adjective, a synonym.

clue.text: Oriental sailor left a mark

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A sailor from the East has left a mark behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascar is the old term for a seaman from India or South-East Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: A spirited harpist?

parts.note: spirited suggests lively, but here it means being a spirit; heavenly beings are pictured playing harps

explanation.surface: A lively musician who plays the harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' means a heavenly spirit, and these are traditionally shown with harps.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly messenger is a spirit conventionally depicted playing the harp on a cloud.

clue.text: Case of foreign wine sent up to college head

indicators.note: the college letter goes at the head, the top of this down entry
in a down clue sent up means the wine's word is written bottom to top

parts.note: retsina is a resin-flavoured Greek wine

explanation.surface: A crate of imported wine is dispatched to the head of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'sent up' reads the Greek wine bottom to top, and 'head' sets the college letter above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal container, a case for holding tea, film or the like.

clue.text: Soldiers on ship have to accept turbulent seas or reconsider

indicators.note: the soldiers-and-ship pair takes in the stirred-up letters of seas
in a down clue, the soldiers sit on top of the ship

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
SS is short for steamship

indicators.note: turbulent seas are churned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops aboard a vessel in rough water have to think again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' gives ASSE, which the soldiers-and-ship pair has to accept between its halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to evaluate it again, so it means think over a second time.

clue.text: Lies in evil sins in beds

indicators.note: the second in places the reworked sins inside the word for beds

parts.note: cots are small beds

indicators.note: evil suggests something twisted, so the letters of sins are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies about wicked sins committed in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies in' looks like lying in bed, but it is the definition, as in 'its charm lies in its simplicity'; 'evil' gives NSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: If a quality lies in something, it is made up of or rests on it, the sense of consists in.

clue.text: Programme that may be debated a long time and amended

parts.note: an age is a very long time

indicators.note: when the word and is amended its letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A plan that is argued over for ages and then altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long time' gives AGE with its own A, and 'amended' gives NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items for discussion at a meeting is its agenda, a schedule of business.

clue.text: Aware of a rising sea but far from queasy

definitions.meaning: sensing a swell, the heaving of the sea: feeling plus swell
in good health and not nauseous: feeling plus well

explanation.surface: A sailor notices the sea getting up but is not seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits two ways: FEELING SWELL and FEELINGS WELL, read as feeling well.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthy and not sick is the plain sense; sensing the heaving waves is the punning sense.

clue.text: Tea and toast

definitions.meaning: to toast someone is to raise a glass to them

explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a beverage, and toasting a person means raising your glass in their honour.

clue.text: Joins forces again, disturbing listeners

indicators.note: disturbing the word listeners knocks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcast about rejoining something upsets the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for the armed services once more is the literal sense of joining forces again.

clue.text: Shamefaced quartet of bluffers?

definitions.meaning: four people who go red with shame
a four-flusher, from poker, is someone who bluffs or pretends

explanation.surface: Four cheats red-faced at being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker a four-flush is four cards of a suit that a player bluffs as a full flush, hence a pretender.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for bluffers and pretenders, from a player faking a flush with four cards.

clue.text: Spotted American inside — kept going

indicators.note: the American abbreviation goes inside the word for spotted

parts.note: something spotted with marks is stained

explanation.surface: A US agent was seen inside and then carried on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like seen, but it means marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintained without stopping over a period, a synonym of continued.

clue.text: He ignores national customs

parts.note: customs suggests traditions, but here it is the border duty service someone evades

explanation.surface: A man who disregards his country's traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' is the government department collecting import duties, not traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings goods across borders illegally avoids paying duty to the authorities.

clue.text: One who doesn't believe a lot can be changed

definitions.text: One who doesn't believe a lot can be changed

parts.words: One who doesn't believe a lot can be changed
parts.note: a lot reads as much, but here it is one's lot in life, one's fate

explanation.surface: A pessimist who thinks little can ever improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like a quantity; it means one's lot, destiny. 'Changed' tempts an anagram, but no fodder fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convinced that destiny is fixed believes their lot is predetermined and unalterable.

clue.text: Usury appears to be very serious

definitions.meaning: usury, lending at unfair interest, is a stingy and miserly trade

explanation.surface: Moneylending at high interest seems a grave matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in earnest and determined; the pun reads it as a miserly line of work.

clue.text: A union measure

definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance, about three miles

explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of groups, and an old unit of distance of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Not a Mr mistaken as Mrs

indicators.note: the letters of not a mr are taken wrongly, put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone who is not Mr has been mistaken for Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a married woman of dignified middle age, which is what the title Mrs suggests.

clue.text: Banks' permits about to expire

definitions.note: the clue reads banks' as banks is, so the definition is the plural noun

indicators.note: the word for permits goes about, around, the word for expire

parts.note: permits are things granted, grants
to expire is to die

explanation.surface: A bank's licences are about to run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks'' looks like financial institutions, but it means slopes, with the apostrophe standing for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks of earth are slopes, and a slope's steepness is its incline.

clue.text: Get used to being in old city quarter

parts.note: being in means present, at home: in
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
E, east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Adapting to life in a district of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to something hard, so they grow used to it.

clue.text: Kipling's wolf emerging from a lake

indicators.note: the name emerges from the letters of a lake, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Kipling wolf climbs out of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the leader of the wolf pack in Kipling's Jungle Book, later the Cub Scout leader's title.

clue.text: Ill stored

definitions.meaning: put away or set aside for later use

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means bedridden with illness, and also means put by in storage, as a ship is out of service.

clue.text: One who hasn't made a score in years

definitions.text: One who hasn't made a score in years

parts.words: One who hasn't made a score in years
parts.note: score suggests a sports result, but here it means twenty: someone not yet twenty years old

explanation.surface: A sportsman who has not scored for years.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; anyone aged thirteen to nineteen has not reached it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged from thirteen to nineteen has not yet reached twenty years of age.

clue.text: He's a right beast!

parts.note: an otter is an animal, a beast

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a man is thoroughly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' here is the British intensifier, as in a right idiot, while also giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad, a nasty and contemptible man, is the old-fashioned British word for a right beast.

clue.text: Club doctor bound leg

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A golf or sports club's medic bandages an injured leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy stick used as a weapon is a club; the word is a synonym.
